prompts.text: What's a small part of your day you genuinely look forward to, even when nothing exciting is planned?
A comfortable conversation about an ordinary day can be more interesting than a grand introduction.
You discover we both take the same route home but notice completely different things. What would you point out first?
A slow Saturday breakfast together or a spontaneous evening walk after a busy day?
Tell me about a tiny routine you picked up from someone and never stopped doing.
A person's favourite part of the morning can tell a surprisingly good story about their habits.
Do you prefer having a bit of quiet before your day starts or jumping straight into whatever needs doing?
Remembering the little things somebody enjoys is often more thoughtful than planning an elaborate surprise.
I mention that my week has been unusually hectic. What's the simplest way you'd suggest unwinding?
Discovering a cosy café together or sitting somewhere outdoors with drinks and no strict schedule?
Which song would you play if you wanted somebody to understand your mood without a long explanation?
Sharing a favourite song is a lovely way to let someone into a small corner of your world.
We're trading three songs each, and the first one I play isn't your style. Do you tell me or politely keep listening?
A playlist made for a long drive or a short collection of songs for a quiet evening?
Tell me about a song you didn't expect to enjoy until somebody played it for you.
Sometimes the story behind a favourite track becomes more interesting than the track itself.
Is there an artist whose music you love but whose songs you'd struggle to recommend to a stranger?
People don't need matching playlists to have fun discovering music together.
We end up at a small live performance neither of us planned to attend. Would you stay for another song?
A live acoustic set in a small room or a relaxed night choosing songs at home?
What's the food you secretly hope somebody suggests whenever nobody knows where to eat?
A simple meal with good conversation can feel more special than an expensive restaurant.
We're choosing a place to eat, and the menu has a dish neither of us recognises. Who asks the waiter about it?
Splitting a few dishes so we can try more flavours or each ordering our own favourite?
Tell me about the last time you tried a new food and immediately wanted another serving.
People are often surprisingly passionate about the correct way to prepare their favourite snack.
Would you rather introduce someone to your favourite meal or discover theirs for the first time?
Being open to a different food recommendation makes even an ordinary outing more memorable.
We stop for a quick bite, but the place has a little queue. What conversation would help the wait pass?
A relaxed breakfast spot or an evening street-food walk where we decide as we go?
What's an outing you'd enjoy even if we only had an hour?
The best first plans give both people room to relax rather than trying to impress each other.
We planned to visit a market, but it closes early. What's your spontaneous alternative?
A bookstore wander followed by coffee or a quick museum visit with lots to discuss afterwards?
Tell me about a day when changing the plan turned out to be the best part.
An unhurried walk can make a new place feel familiar very quickly.
Do you like choosing a place to meet together or having someone suggest a couple of options?
Plans feel more inviting when either person can honestly say something isn't their thing.
I suggest an activity you've never tried, but you're not sure you'll enjoy it. What would help you decide?
Trying a completely new neighbourhood together or returning to a favourite spot to show me why you like it?
What's a harmless habit your friends love teasing you about?
Being able to laugh at a small mistake makes a conversation feel comfortable.
I confidently pronounce a common word the wrong way, and you notice. Do you correct me or enjoy the moment?
A conversation full of ridiculous hypotheticals or one where we trade embarrassing but funny stories?
Tell me about something that wasn't funny at the time but makes you laugh now.
Some people tell their funniest stories without realising how funny they sound.
Are you the person who makes terrible puns or the one who groans and secretly enjoys them?
Shared humour doesn't mean finding every single joke funny.
We're playing a board game and I lose spectacularly. What's your acceptable level of teasing?
Watching a clever comedy together or finding out which old internet jokes still make each other laugh?
What's something small somebody noticed about you that genuinely surprised you?
A person remembering an ordinary preference can make a stronger impression than a big speech.
You mention a book you'd like to read, and I remember its title weeks later. Would that stand out to you?
Someone remembering the kind of drink you like or remembering a story you told them?
Tell me about a thoughtful gesture you still remember because it came at the right moment.
Paying attention is often less about grand gestures and more about listening properly.
Is there a little courtesy that immediately helps you feel comfortable around somebody?
Being considerate doesn't require trying to guess everything another person wants.
We're meeting after work and you've had a long day. Would you prefer a quieter plan or a change of scenery?
A thoughtful message after meeting up or a small surprise recommendation based on something you mentioned?
What's a film you love that you suspect I'd have a completely different opinion about?
Having different tastes can make getting to know somebody much more interesting.
You recommend a series I don't enjoy after two episodes. Should I give it another chance or report back honestly?
Watching each other's favourite film or choosing something neither person has seen before?
Tell me about a recommendation you initially dismissed and later loved.
Two people can have opposite reactions to the same ending and still enjoy discussing it.
Is there an activity you think most people overlook until somebody introduces them to it?
A gentle disagreement can be good conversation if nobody treats it as a competition.
I insist that rainy evenings are better than sunny afternoons. What's your counterargument?
Finding out how similar our tastes are or discovering a few differences that make us laugh?
Do you prefer little updates during the day or one proper catch-up when you're free?
A meaningful message doesn't need to arrive immediately to be worth receiving.
I send you a photograph of something that reminded me of our conversation. What kind of picture would you send back?
Exchanging short voice notes or having an occasional long phone conversation?
Tell me about an unexpected message that made an otherwise ordinary day better.
Some conversations stay enjoyable because nobody feels they have to force the next topic.
What makes a phone call feel easy rather than like something you need to prepare for?
Knowing when someone is busy can make communication more relaxed for both people.
We're midway through an interesting conversation when you have to leave. How would you like to pick it up later?
A spontaneous 'this reminded me of you' message or a planned call when we're both free?
What's something you'd like to get better at purely because you think you'd enjoy it?
The little projects people do for themselves are often more revealing than their formal job titles.
You tell me you're learning a new skill and making slow progress. Would encouragement or a curious question be more useful?
Trying a creative class together or swapping updates on the personal projects we're each working on?
Tell me about a small goal that turned out to matter more to you than you expected.
Some ambitions start as casual ideas people mention while talking about their weekend.
Have you ever become interested in a hobby because of a conversation with someone?
It's nice when somebody can talk about their ambitions without feeling they have to sound impressive.
We each choose one unfamiliar activity to try before the end of the month. How would you decide on yours?
Learning how to make something by hand or taking a short class on a topic you know nothing about?
What usually helps you relax when you're spending time with someone you're still getting to know?
A comfortable silence can be a good sign without needing to mean anything dramatic.
We run into each other unexpectedly while doing errands. Do you suggest a quick chat or keep to our separate plans?
An easy conversation while doing something together or a quiet spot where we can just talk?
Tell me about a time somebody made you feel welcome without making a fuss.
The best part of getting to know a person is often discovering which little things make them laugh.
Do you usually warm up to people quickly, or does familiarity grow with a few ordinary conversations?
Getting to know someone at a natural pace is more pleasant than turning every meeting into a big occasion.
We spend an afternoon together and realise neither of us checked the time. What kind of outing probably led to that?
Having a clear plan for our next catch-up or leaving room for a simple last-minute idea?
